page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What it is
steps.why: After the growth plates close the long bones can no longer lengthen, so extra growth hormone thickens the bones instead.
common_mistakes: Naming gigantism. That is the same excess before adulthood.
Naming thyroxine. The hormone is growth hormone.
steps.memory_tip: Acro means extremities: the hands, feet and jaw thicken.
steps.margin_note: Name the hormone in the first line.
lines: Acromegaly is a hormonal disorder caused

steps.label: Its signs
steps.why: Only the parts that can still thicken change, which is why the jaw, hands and feet are affected and the height is not.
common_mistakes: Saying the person grows taller. In adults the height does not change.
steps.memory_tip: Jaw, hands and feet enlarge; the height stays the same.
steps.margin_note: Two or three named signs are enough.
lines: The bones of the jaw, hands and feet
enlarge. The nose, lips and eyelids thicken

lines.text: and the finger tips become wide

insider_note: Two things are asked: the disorder and the hormone. Name growth hormone explicitly, and say 'in adults' — the same excess in a child gives gigantism instead.
